entry.title: Venture Capitalists Push Up AI Startup Valuations With Tranched Two-Step Rounds
entry.content:
Techmeme | bloomberg.com

Venture capitalists are increasingly utilizing tranched, two-step funding rounds to back early-stage artificial intelligence startups at rapidly escalating valuations. This mechanism involves structuring a single fundraising round into distinct tranches—an initial lower-priced slice followed by a follow-on tranche priced significantly higher—allowing multiple investors to participate at different price points.

This practice has been highlighted by intense investor competition for nascent companies like Emulate, a three-month-old AI startup founded by Google DeepMind alumni that secured a multi-billion-dollar valuation despite lacking a public product or website. While these structures allow founders to raise unprecedented amounts of capital and headline valuations quickly, they also complicate market assessments of actual startup worth.

entry.content:
TechCrunch AI | techcrunch.com

Eka Robotics has closed a $150 million Series A funding round led by Andreessen Horowitz and F-Prime, bringing its post-money valuation to $1.45 billion. The startup develops a physical AI model and a force-sensitive gripper designed to improve robotic dexterity and manipulation tasks through reinforcement learning and simulation.

Founded by MIT professor Pulkit Agrawal and former Google DeepMind researcher Tuomas Haarnoja, Eka utilizes a vision-force-action architecture rather than traditional vision-language-action models to handle physical interactions. While the company demonstrates high-speed pick-and-place capabilities in controlled environments, it faces the ongoing challenge of scaling its hardware and proving long-term reliability across industrial assembly lines.
